results.detailed_description:
Gen 8 now holds two grippers. On the left is the Grabette, the hand-held one. On the right is the Gripette, the robot gripper. Both come straight from Pollen's own files at the same commit, with nothing redesigned. Explode works on both, and the slider opens and closes both fingers. A check confirms each finger lands within 0.01 mm of where Pollen's design puts it.

How they're driven. The Grabette has no motor. You hold the handle and close its one finger yourself against the fixed thumb. To measure the grip, a small magnet sits at each finger joint. A magnetic angle sensor board (AS5600L) rides on the finger over each magnet and reads that joint's angle about 90 times a second.

The Gripette has no gears or linkage. It uses two Feetech STS3215 servos. Servo 1 sits in the base, and its horn bolts straight onto the finger, so it swings the whole finger. Servo 2 rides on the finger, and its horn bolts straight onto the tip, so it bends the tip. The joints match the Grabette's, which is how Pollen's teleop drives a Gripette live from a Grabette, sensor to servo.

Labels: the viewer can't show text on parts, so I coloured them. The servos are magenta and the sensors and magnets are red. Everything else keeps Pollen's colours. They sit inside the shells, so tap Explode to see them, or look at previews/drive.png. The slider moves only the base joint, and the tips stay straight.

results.identified_issue: Source: packages/grabette/urdf/grabette_right/ at b5bacab06c19 (onshape-to-robot output). export_models.py does URDF forward kinematics (rpy = Rz*Ry*Rx). WORLD maps URDF (x,y,z)->(-x,-z,-y) mm, so the proximal joint axis becomes world Y about the origin, and the poses.js hinge {match ^Finger, pivot 0, sign +1, exported 90} reproduces FK; check_geometry.py verifies this. Gallery angle = proximal_deg + 90 (URDF limits [-90,0], 0 = open). Distal joint fixed at 0. Explode offsets are heuristic: 0.9*(part bbox centre - group centre), plus 0.6*(group centre - body centre) for finger groups. STLs are gitignored, so a fresh checkout needs fetch_grabette.py, which caches the clone in ~/HelpingHands-tools/cache/grabette. Uncommitted local edits (untracked files owned by others): Scripts/publish_designs.py generations map (+v008 -> 8), Two Finger Gripper/README.md, references/generalist/GENERATIONS.txt. Scripts/check_gripper_closure.py skips Gen 8 because it pairs hinges two at a time and Gen 8 has one; its existing FAILs for Gens 1-7 were already there. Chose the full grabette_right URDF (37 meshes) over the *_viewer variant (30 meshes) because it is the complete assembly.
results.summary: Gen 8 is now Pollen's real Grabette, built from their own files. It opens in the gallery, and Explode and the open/close slider both work.
results.detailed_description:
Gen 8 is exactly the Grabette, with no merging and no redesign. I took Pollen's right-hand Grabette files (github.com/pollen-robotics/grabette, pinned to commit b5bacab, Apache-2.0). Then I put each of their 73 parts where their own URDF puts it: shell, grip, Raspberry Pi and box, OAK-D camera, battery, fisheye camera, every screw, the finger and the soft tips. No shape was changed. The only change is turning the whole model so it sits upright in the viewer.

It's live in the gallery as Gen 8. Tap Explode and the parts fly apart by sub-assembly (body, finger, tip). The slider closes the one moving finger against the fixed thumb, just as Pollen's joint does, from 79 mm open to tips touching. A check confirms the slider puts every finger part within 0.01 mm of where Pollen's URDF says it goes.

Licence: Pollen's LICENSE, NOTICE and third-party notices are copied in unchanged next to the files. One thing to know: their 37 meshes (34 MB) aren't committed, because this repo ignores .stl files. Running fetch_grabette.py brings them back byte-for-byte from Pollen's repo. It checks every file against a recorded fingerprint, so it fails loudly if upstream ever changes. The tip's passive flex joint is held straight. To show Gen 8 in the gallery, I also added one line to Scripts/publish_designs.py and pointed the Two Finger Gripper README at Gen 8. Both files are untracked local files I didn't create, so those edits aren't committed.
